Telangiectasias in the gastrointestinal tract are common in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified ANGPT2 inhibition as a potential therapy for the treatment of AVMs in hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia patients.

we identified the angiopoiein-Tek signaling as a potential therapeutic target for hereditary hemorrhage telangiectasia (HHT) patients, and we showed that ANGPT2 inhibition in Smad4 HHT mouse model alleviates AVMs.
the TGFβ pathway is a key regulator of angiopoietin signaling in the context of hereditary hemorrhage telangiectasia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TGFβ downstream effector, SMAD4, regulates the transcriptional activation of ANGPT-2, which is a ligand that binds to a receptor called TEK (also known as TIE-2).
the TGFβ pathway is a critical regulator of angiopoietin-1/angiopoietin 2 balance in endothelial cells.
the loss of SmAd4 in endothelial cells causes an increase in Angiopoietin 2, a pro-angiogenic factor that is involved in the formation of arteriovenous shunts.
